## Pages

### `Page`

```python
Page(document: Document, number: int, generation: int)
```

A page of a document, named by its page object.

A page stays the same page when other pages are inserted, moved, or
deleted; `index` follows it. Once the page itself is deleted, its
reads raise `StalePageError`, and they work again if undo
restores it. Two pages are equal when they name the same page object of
the same document.

- `document`: Return the document that holds the page.
- `xref`: Return the object number of the page dictionary.
- `obj`: Return the page dictionary as a handle of the low-level object model.
- `annotations`: Return the page's annotations other than links and form widgets, in `/Annots` order.
- `links`: Return the page's link annotations, in `/Annots` order.
- `widgets`: Return the page's form widgets, in `/Annots` order.
- `index`: Return the zero-based index of the page, in time that does not grow with the page count.
- `images(*, annotations: bool = True) -> list[PageImage]`: Return the images that the page paints, in the paint order of `content`.
- `label`: Return the page's label from `doc.page_labels`, or `""` when no range covers it.
- `rotation` (settable): Return the page's `/Rotate`, inherited and normalized to 0, 90, 180, or 270.
- `rect`: Return the display `Rect` `(0, 0, width, height)`, with the rotation applied.
- `media_box` (settable): Return the page's MediaBox in display space, inherited, or the A4 page that the renderer draws.
- `crop_box` (settable): Return the page's CropBox in display space: inherited, clipped to the MediaBox, and the MediaBox when absent.
- `bleed_box` (settable): Return the page's BleedBox in display space, clipped to the MediaBox, and the CropBox when absent.
- `trim_box` (settable): Return the page's TrimBox in display space, clipped to the MediaBox, and the CropBox when absent.
- `art_box` (settable): Return the page's ArtBox in display space, clipped to the MediaBox, and the CropBox when absent.
- `pixmap(*, dpi: float | None = None, matrix: Sequence[float] | None = None, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, alpha: bool = False, background: tuple[int, int, int] | tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None, annotations: bool = True, colorspace: Colorspace | Literal['gray', 'rgb'] = <Colorspace.RGB: 'rgb'>) -> Pixmap`: Render the current version of the page to a `Pixmap`.
- `flatten(*, annotations: bool = True, widgets: bool = True)`: Draw this page's annotation and widget appearances into its content and take them off.
- `ocr(*, engine: OcrEngine | None = None, dpi: float = 300, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, rotation: OcrRotation = 0, tile_size: int = 1408, overlap: int = 192, min_confidence: float = 0.5) -> list[OcrWord]`: Recognize the rendered page's text without changing the document.
- `apply_ocr(*, words: Iterable[OcrWord] | None = None, engine: OcrEngine | None = None, dpi: float = 300, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, rotation: OcrRotation = 0, skip_existing: bool = True, tile_size: int = 1408, overlap: int = 192, min_confidence: float = 0.5) -> list[OcrWord]`: Add an invisible, searchable text layer and return the words it holds.
- `svg(*, annotations: bool = True, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> str`: Render the current version of the page to an SVG string at 72 dpi, with text drawn as paths.
- `content(*, text_runs: bool = True, paths: bool = True, images: bool = True, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, annotations: bool = True, max_elements: int | None = 262144) -> Content`: Return the text runs, paths, and images that the page paints.
- `text(*, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, clipped: bool = False, ligatures: bool = True, whitespace: bool = True, dehyphenate: bool = False, unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip', max_glyphs: int | None = 262144, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> str`: Return the text of the current version of the page in reading order.
- `words(*, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, clipped: bool = False, ligatures: bool = True, whitespace: bool = True, dehyphenate: bool = False, unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip', exact_bboxes: bool = False, max_glyphs: int | None = 262144, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> list[Word]`: Return the words of the current version of the page in reading order, as `Word` records.
- `layout(*, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, chars: bool = False, clipped: bool = False, ligatures: bool = True, whitespace: bool = True, dehyphenate: bool = False, unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip', exact_bboxes: bool = False, styles: bool = False, max_glyphs: int | None = 262144, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> Layout`: Return the text of the current version of the page as blocks, lines, and spans, in reading order.
- `chars(*, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, clipped: bool = False, ligatures: bool = True, whitespace: bool = True, dehyphenate: bool = False, unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip', exact_bboxes: bool = False, styles: bool = False, max_glyphs: int | None = 262144, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> Chars`: Return the chars of the current version of the page as `Chars` columns, in layout order.
- `search(text: str, *, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, quads: bool = False, max_hits: int | None = 4096, clipped: bool = False, ligatures: bool = True, whitespace: bool = True, dehyphenate: bool = False, unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip', exact_bboxes: bool = False, max_glyphs: int | None = 262144, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> list[Rect] | list[Quad]`: Search the text of the current version of the page case-insensitively for `text`.
- `selection(start: Sequence[float], end: Sequence[float], *, clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, max_glyphs: int | None = 262144, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> str`: Return the text that a viewer selects by dragging from `start` to `end`.
- `markdown(*, table_strategy: Literal['lines', 'text'] | None = 'lines', max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> str`: Return the current version of the page as Markdown.
- `tables(*, strategy: Literal['lines', 'text'] = 'lines', clip: Sequence[float] | None = None, max_glyphs: int | None = 262144, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> list[Table]`: Find the tables of the current version of the page from vector rules or aligned text.
- `operations` (settable): Return the page's content as `Operations`, as hayro reads it.

### `Pages`

```python
Pages(document: Document)
```

The pages of a document, in order.

Indexing, slicing, and iteration give `Page` handles, which keep
naming their pages through later edits. `new`, `insert`,
`del`, `select`, and `move` each change the page tree in
one transaction.

- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of pages.
- `labeled(label: str) -> list[int]`: Return the indexes of the pages whose page label is `label`.
- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Page | list[Page]`: Return page `index`, or a list of the pages of a slice.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[Page]`: Iterate over the pages; a structural edit during the iteration raises `RuntimeError`.
- `index(page: object, start: int = 0, stop: int | None = None) -> int`: Return the index of `page`, in time that does not grow with the page count.
- `new(size: tuple[float, float] = (595.0, 842.0), *, index: int | None = None) -> Page`: Add a blank page of `size` points, A4 by default, where `list.insert` would put it.
- `insert(index: int, pages: Page | Iterable[Page])`: Insert copies of `pages` before `index`, clamped as `list.insert` clamps it, in one transaction.
- `extend(pages: Page | Iterable[Page])`: Append copies of `pages`, as `insert` at the end inserts them.
- `select(indexes: Iterable[int], /)`: Keep the pages at `indexes`, in that order, and remove the others, in one transaction.
- `move(index: int, to: int)`: Move page `index` so that it ends at index `to`, in one transaction.

## Text and content

### `BlendMode`

A blend mode of ISO 32000-2 §11.3.5.

Members: `NORMAL`, `MULTIPLY`, `SCREEN`, `OVERLAY`, `DARKEN`, `LIGHTEN`, `COLOR_DODGE`, `COLOR_BURN`, `HARD_LIGHT`, `SOFT_LIGHT`, `DIFFERENCE`, `EXCLUSION`, `HUE`, `SATURATION`, `COLOR`, `LUMINOSITY`.

### `Block`

```python
Block(*, text: str, bbox: Rect, lines: tuple[Line, ...])
```

A block of lines of a `Layout`; `text` joins the lines with newlines.

### `Char`

```python
Char(*, text: str, bbox: Rect, origin: Point, is_synthetic: bool = False, stream: int | None = None, operation: int | None = None)
```

One glyph of a `Span`, from `Page.layout` with `chars=True`.

`text` is the glyph's complete Unicode mapping, which can hold several
characters, such as the two of an `fi` ligature. `origin` is its point
on the baseline; `bbox` spans the glyph's advance and the font's
ascender and descender, or its outline with `exact_bboxes=True`.

### `Chars`

```python
Chars(columns: CharColumns, start: int = 0, stop: int | None = None)
```

The chars of a page as columns, from `Page.chars` and `Layout.chars`.

Each row is one `Char` of the layout with chars, in layout order,
and the row view builds that record on demand: `len(chars)`,
`chars[i]`, and iteration give records equal to the spans' `chars`.
A slice with a step of 1 is a view of the same columns.

`column` returns each column without a copy as a read-only
`memoryview`, which `numpy.frombuffer` reads; its items are in the
machine's byte order. The columns are those of `names`:

- `x0`, `y0`, `x1`, `y1` (float64): `Char.bbox`;
- `origin_x`, `origin_y` (float64): `Char.origin`;
- `text_offsets` (int32, one more than the rows) and `text_data`
  (bytes): the UTF-8 of every `Char.text`, which row `i` holds from
  `text_offsets[i]` to `text_offsets[i + 1]` of `text_data`, as
  Arrow's `utf8` holds it. A view shares the `text_data` of the
  whole page;
- `block`, `line`, `span` (uint32): the row's place in
  `Layout.blocks`, its block's `lines`, and its line's `spans`;
- `is_synthetic` (uint8, 0 or 1): `Char.is_synthetic`;
- `stream`, `operation` (uint32): `Char.stream` and
  `Char.operation`, both 0 where they are `None`. No object has
  the number 0, so `stream == 0` marks those rows.

The table is also an Arrow struct array through the Arrow PyCapsule
interface, which pyarrow, polars, and DuckDB import without a copy. Its
fields are those of the columns, with one `text` field (`utf8`) for
`text_offsets` and `text_data`, `is_synthetic` as Arrow
booleans, and `stream` and `operation` null where they are `None`.

- `__len__() -> int`
- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Char | Chars`
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[Char]`
- `column(name: str) -> memoryview`: Return the column `name` of `names` as a read-only `memoryview`, without a copy.

### `Clip`

```python
Clip(*, segments: tuple[Segment, ...], fill_rule: FillRule, bbox: Rect)
```

A clipping path in display space.

### `ClosePath`

```python
ClosePath()
```

Close the current subpath with a line to its start.

### `Color`

```python
Color(red: float, green: float, blue: float, alpha: float = 1.0)
```

A solid paint, as the sRGB color and alpha that hayro converts it to.

Components range from 0 to 1. The color space and its own components
are not exposed yet.

- `rgb`: Return `(red, green, blue)`.

### `Content`

```python
Content(items: tuple[ContentItem, ...])
```

The items that a page paints, in paint order.

- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> ContentItem | tuple[ContentItem, ...]`: Return one item, or a tuple of items for a slice.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of items.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[ContentItem]`: Iterate over the items in paint order.
- `text_runs`: Return the text runs in paint order.
- `paths`: Return the paths in paint order.
- `images`: Return the images in paint order.
- `path_clusters(*, x_tolerance: float = 3, y_tolerance: float = 3) -> list[Rect]`: Return the boxes of the groups of paths that lie near one another.

### `ContentItem`

`ContentItem = pyropdf.TextRun | pyropdf.Path | pyropdf.Image`

### `CurveTo`

```python
CurveTo(c1: Point, c2: Point, to: Point)
```

Draw a cubic Bézier curve to `to` with two control points.

### `FillRule`

The rule that decides which areas a path fills or clips.

Members: `NONZERO`, `EVEN_ODD`.

### `FontRef`

```python
FontRef(*, name: str, is_type3: bool, weight: int | None, is_italic: bool, is_serif: bool, is_monospace: bool)
```

The font that a text run uses, as hayro reads its font program.

The font dictionary's object number, subtype, and embedding are not
exposed yet. All Type 3 fonts share one reference.

### `Glyph`

```python
Glyph(*, glyph_id: int | None, text: str | None, matrix: Matrix, advance: float | None, bbox: Rect | None)
```

One glyph of a text run.

- `origin`: Return the glyph origin on the baseline.
- `size`: Return the display-space font size.

### `GraphicsContext`

```python
GraphicsContext(*, clips: tuple[Clip, ...], groups: tuple[TransparencyGroup, ...], marked_content: tuple[MarkedContent, ...])
```

The clips, transparency groups, and marked content around an item.

Each tuple lists its entries outermost first.

- `opacity`: Return the product of the groups' opacities.
- `clip_bbox`: Return the intersection of the clips' boxes, or `None` without clips.

### `Image`

```python
Image(*, xref: int, width: int, height: int, bits: int, colorspace: str, components: int, is_stencil: bool, mask: ImageMask | None, encoded_size: int, resolution: tuple[int, int], matrix: Matrix, bbox: Rect, context: GraphicsContext, blend_mode: BlendMode, soft_mask: SoftMask | None)
```

An image painted on the page.

### `ImageMask`

The kind of mask that an image dictionary names.

Members: `SOFT`, `EXPLICIT`, `COLOR_KEY`.

### `Layout`

```python
Layout(*, width: float, height: float, blocks: tuple[Block, ...], chars: Chars | None = None)
```

The text of a page as blocks, lines, spans, and, on request, characters.

`width` and `height` are those of the page's display box; every box
is in display space.

- `to_dict() -> dict[str, Any]`: Return the layout as dictionaries, lists, and tuples for JSON.
- `to_html() -> str`: Return the layout as a positioned HTML fragment, as pymupdf's `"html"` output.
- `to_xml() -> str`: Return the layout as XML, as pymupdf's `"xml"` output.

### `Line`

```python
Line(*, text: str, bbox: Rect, direction: Point, is_vertical: bool, spans: tuple[Span, ...], quad: Quad)
```

A line of a `Block`.

`text` joins the line's words with single spaces. `direction` is the
unit vector of the baseline in display space, `(1, 0)` for horizontal
text, and `is_vertical` is true for vertical writing, in which glyphs
stack downward.

### `LineCap`

The shape at the open ends of a stroke.

Members: `BUTT`, `ROUND`, `SQUARE`.

### `LineJoin`

The shape at the corners of a stroke.

Members: `MITER`, `ROUND`, `BEVEL`.

### `LineTo`

```python
LineTo(to: Point)
```

Draw a line to `to`.

### `MarkedContent`

```python
MarkedContent(*, tag: str, mcid: int | None)
```

A marked-content sequence (`BMC` or `BDC`).

### `MoveTo`

```python
MoveTo(to: Point)
```

Start a new subpath at `to`.

### `Paint`

`Paint = pyropdf.Color | pyropdf.ShadingPattern | pyropdf.TilingPattern`

### `Path`

```python
Path(*, segments: tuple[Segment, ...], fill: Paint | None, fill_rule: FillRule, stroke: Stroke | None, bbox: Rect, context: GraphicsContext, blend_mode: BlendMode, soft_mask: SoftMask | None)
```

A path that is filled, stroked, or both.

### `Segment`

`Segment = pyropdf.MoveTo | pyropdf.LineTo | pyropdf.CurveTo | pyropdf.ClosePath`

### `ShadingPattern`

```python
ShadingPattern(*, shading_type: ShadingType | None, matrix: Matrix, opacity: float)
```

A paint that a shading fills, from a shading pattern or `sh`.

### `ShadingType`

A shading type of ISO 32000-2 §8.7.4.5.

hayro reads free-form and lattice-form triangle meshes (types 4 and 5)
into the same triangles, so both report `TRIANGLE_MESH`.

Members: `FUNCTION`, `AXIAL`, `RADIAL`, `TRIANGLE_MESH`, `COONS_PATCH_MESH`, `TENSOR_PATCH_MESH`.

### `SoftMask`

```python
SoftMask(*, xref: int, subtype: SoftMaskType)
```

A soft mask: the transparency group that masks what it encloses.

### `SoftMaskType`

What a soft mask reads from its group: alpha or luminosity.

Members: `ALPHA`, `LUMINOSITY`.

### `Span`

```python
Span(*, text: str, bbox: Rect, origin: Point, size: float, font: str, is_bold: bool, is_italic: bool, is_serif: bool, is_monospaced: bool, is_superscript: bool, is_underlined: bool, is_struck: bool, color: Color | None, render_mode: TextRenderMode, is_clipped: bool, ascender: float, descender: float, chars: tuple[Char, ...], quad: Quad)
```

A run of text in one font, size, paint, and render mode within a `Line`.

`origin` is the baseline point of the first glyph. `chars` holds the
glyphs when `Page.layout` was called with `chars=True` and is empty
otherwise.

### `Stroke`

```python
Stroke(*, paint: Paint, width: float = 1.0, cap: LineCap = <LineCap.BUTT: 'butt'>, join: LineJoin = <LineJoin.MITER: 'miter'>, miter_limit: float = 10.0, dashes: tuple[float, ...] = (), dash_offset: float = 0.0)
```

How a path or text run is stroked, in display space.

`width` and the dash lengths are scaled by the largest scale of the
transform in force when the stroke was painted.

### `Table`

```python
Table(*, bbox: Rect, rows: tuple[tuple[str | None, ...], ...], cells: tuple[tuple[Rect | None, ...], ...], diagnostics: TableDiagnostics, _anchors: tuple[int, ...] | None = None)
```

A table that `Page.tables` detected, in display space.

`rows` holds the text of every cell and `cells` its box, both row by
row. A merged cell keeps its text and its spanning box in its top-left
slot; the slots it covers are `None`.

- `markdown(*, fill_empty: bool = True, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> str`: Return the table as Markdown, with the first row as its header.

### `TableDiagnostics`

```python
TableDiagnostics(*, strategy: Literal['lines', 'text'], confidence: float, alignment_error_em: float | None, minimum_gutter_em: float | None, row_gap_variation_em: float | None)
```

The geometric evidence for one detected table.

`confidence` ranks the results of this deterministic detector from 0
to 1; it is not a probability. The metrics in ems are present for the
`"text"` strategy and `None` for vector grids.

### `TextRenderMode`

How a text run paints its glyphs.

hayro paints the clipping modes 4 to 6 as their painting part and adds
their clip to the context of later items; text in mode 7, which only
clips, paints nothing and is not an item.

Members: `FILL`, `STROKE`, `FILL_STROKE`, `INVISIBLE`.

### `TextRun`

```python
TextRun(*, glyphs: tuple[Glyph, ...], font: FontRef, render_mode: TextRenderMode, fill: Paint | None, stroke: Stroke | None, bbox: Rect, context: GraphicsContext, blend_mode: BlendMode, soft_mask: SoftMask | None)
```

The glyphs that one text-showing operator paints.

- `text`: Return the Unicode text of the glyphs that map to one.
- `size`: Return the display-space font size of the first glyph.

### `TilingPattern`

```python
TilingPattern(*, bbox: Rect, x_step: float, y_step: float, matrix: Matrix)
```

A paint that repeats a pattern cell.

### `TransparencyGroup`

```python
TransparencyGroup(*, opacity: float, blend_mode: BlendMode, soft_mask: SoftMask | None)
```

A transparency group and what it applies to everything inside it.

### `Unmapped`

`Unmapped = typing.Literal['skip', 'replacement', 'glyph_id']`

### `Word`

```python
Word(*, text: str, bbox: Rect, block: int, line: int, index: int)
```

One word of `Page.words`, in reading order.

`block` and `line` are the indexes of the `Block` of
`Page.layout` that holds the word and of the `Line` in it, and
`index` is the word's position in that line.

## OCR

### `OcrEngine`

```python
OcrEngine(detector_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, recognizer_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, dictionary_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, *, threads: int | None = None, max_concurrent: int = 1, max_model_size: int | None = 67108864)
```

Reusable, pure-Rust PP-OCR engine.

With no paths, the engine discovers models from the optional
`pyropdf[ocr]` installation. Explicit paths are useful for evaluating a
compatible RTen-format PP-OCR detector, recognizer, and character
dictionary.

- `recognize(pixmap: Pixmap, *, tile_size: int = 1408, overlap: int = 192, min_confidence: float = 0.5, rotation: OcrRotation = 0) -> list[OcrWord]`: Recognize text in any `Pixmap`.

### `OcrRotation`

`OcrRotation = typing.Literal[0, 90, 180, 270]`

### `OcrWord`

```python
OcrWord(*, text: str, bbox: Rect, confidence: float)
```

One recognized word: its text, its box, and the engine's confidence from 0 to 1.

`Page.ocr` and `Page.apply_ocr` give boxes in the page's
display space and `OcrEngine.recognize` in the pixmap's pixels.
Words that another OCR engine recognized go to `Page.apply_ocr` as
`OcrWord` records in display space.

## Rendering

### `Colorspace`

The color space of a `Pixmap`'s samples.

Members: `GRAY`, `RGB`.

### `Pixmap`

A rendered page: immutable pixels, row by row from the top, RGB or gray,
each with or without straight alpha, 8 bits per channel.

- `alpha`: Whether each pixel ends with a straight alpha byte.
- `channels`: Bytes per pixel: 1 for gray, 3 for RGB, and one more with alpha.
- `colorspace`: The color space of the samples, a `pyropdf.Colorspace`.
- `height`: Height in pixels.
- `resolution`: The horizontal and vertical resolution in dots per inch, which PNG output records.
- `save(path, /, *, format=None, quality=...)`: Writes the pixels as `format`, `"png"` or `"jpeg"` at `quality`, or else the format that the extension of `path` names, and replaces `path` atomically after a complete write, keeping an existing file's permissions and a final symlink. A failed save leaves `path` as it was.
- `stride`: Bytes per row: width × channels.
- `to_bytes(format='png', *, quality=..., max_size=...)`: Returns the pixels encoded as `format`, `"png"` or `"jpeg"` at `quality`, 1 through 100. JPEG has no alpha.
- `width`: Width in pixels.

## Annotations

### `Annotation`

```python
Annotation(page: Page, id: tuple[int, int], index: int)
```

A handle on one annotation of a page, as `page.annotations` lists it.

Properties read the document on every access. A handle names the
annotation's object, so it finds the annotation again after an edit
moved it; one stored as a direct dictionary in `/Annots` is found by
its position. A handle raises `StaleObjectError` while the
annotation is not on its page, and `StalePageError` while the
page is gone; it works again if undo restores them.

- `page`: Return the page that holds the annotation.
- `xref`: Return the annotation's object number, or 0 for a dictionary stored in `/Annots` itself.
- `obj`: Return the annotation dictionary as a live low-level handle.
- `type`: Return the annotation type, `AnnotationType.UNKNOWN` for a subtype pyropdf does not know.
- `rect` (settable): Return or set the annotation rectangle in display coordinates.
- `contents` (settable): Return or set the text that the annotation shows or describes, `/Contents`.
- `author` (settable): Return or set the author, `/T`.
- `subject` (settable): Return or set the subject, `/Subj`.
- `created`: Return the creation date as the PDF date string stored, `/CreationDate`.
- `modified`: Return the modification date as the PDF date string stored, `/M`.
- `name` (settable): Return or set the annotation's unique name on its page, `/NM`.
- `icon` (settable): Return or set the icon name of a note, stamp, or file attachment, `/Name`.
- `intent`: Return the intent, `/IT`, such as `"FreeTextCallout"`.
- `color` (settable): Return or set the color of the border, title bar, or text markup, `/C`; CMYK converts to RGB.
- `interior_color` (settable): Return or set the fill color of a shape or line ending, `/IC`; CMYK converts to RGB.
- `opacity` (settable): Return or set the constant opacity, `/CA`, 1.0 when absent.
- `flags` (settable): Return or set the `/F` flags.
- `border` (settable): Return or set the border that `/BS`, else `/Border`, describes, or `None` without either.
- `clouds` (settable): Return or set the intensity of a cloudy border, `/BE`, from 0 (none) to 2.
- `blend_mode` (settable): Return or set the blend mode that the appearance is drawn with, `/BM`, or `None` without one.
- `vertices` (settable): Return or set the display points of a line (its two ends), polygon, or polyline.
- `strokes` (settable): Return or set the display points of each stroke of an ink annotation, `None` for another type.
- `line_endings` (settable): Return or set the start and end shapes of a line or polyline, `None` for another type.
- `rotation` (settable): Return or set how far the annotation's content is turned clockwise as the page is displayed.
- `language` (settable): Return or set the BCP 47 language of the annotation's text, `/Lang`; `del` removes it.
- `popup_rect` (settable): Return or set the display rectangle of the annotation's popup, `None` without one.
- `is_open` (settable): Return or set whether the popup, or a note without one, opens when the page is shown.
- `in_reply_to` (settable): Return or set the annotation that this one replies to, `/IRT`, or `None`.
- `replies`: Return the annotations of the page that reply to this one, in `/Annots` order.

### `AnnotationFlags`

Annotation `/F` flags (ISO 32000-2 Table 167); the values are pymupdf's `PDF_ANNOT_IS_*`.

Members: `INVISIBLE`, `HIDDEN`, `PRINT`, `NO_ZOOM`, `NO_ROTATE`, `NO_VIEW`, `READ_ONLY`, `LOCKED`, `TOGGLE_NO_VIEW`, `LOCKED_CONTENTS`.

### `Annotations`

```python
Annotations(page: Page)
```

The annotations of a page other than links and form widgets, as `page.annotations` returns them.

The sequence lists them in `/Annots` order and reads the page on every
access; popups belong to the annotation that names them and are not
listed. `del page.annotations[i]` removes one, with its popup.

Reads reject more than 4,096 annotations or 1 MiB of annotation text per
page.

- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Annotation | list[Annotation]`: Return one annotation, or a list of them for a slice.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of annotations on the page.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[Annotation]`: Iterate over the annotations that the page lists now.
- `add(specification: AnnotationSpecification) -> Annotation`: Add the annotation that `specification` describes, and return it.

### `AnnotationSpecification`

`AnnotationSpecification = pyropdf.Highlight | pyropdf.Underline | pyropdf.StrikeOut | pyropdf.Squiggly | pyropdf.Note | pyropdf.Square | pyropdf.Circle | pyropdf.LineAnnotation | pyropdf.Polygon | pyropdf.PolyLine | pyropdf.Ink`

### `AnnotationType`

Annotation types by `/Subtype`; the values are pymupdf's `PDF_ANNOT_*` codes.

Members: `UNKNOWN`, `TEXT`, `LINK`, `FREE_TEXT`, `LINE`, `SQUARE`, `CIRCLE`, `POLYGON`, `POLY_LINE`, `HIGHLIGHT`, `UNDERLINE`, `SQUIGGLY`, `STRIKE_OUT`, `REDACT`, `STAMP`, `CARET`, `INK`, `POPUP`, `FILE_ATTACHMENT`, `SOUND`, `MOVIE`, `RICH_MEDIA`, `WIDGET`, `SCREEN`, `PRINTER_MARK`, `TRAP_NET`, `WATERMARK`, `THREE_D`, `PROJECTION`.

### `AttachmentIcon`

The icon of a file attachment, `/Name` (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.15).

Members: `GRAPH`, `PUSH_PIN`, `PAPERCLIP`, `TAG`.

### `Border`

```python
Border(width: float = 1.0, *, style: BorderStyle | None = None, dashes: Sequence[float] = ())
```

The border of an annotation: its line width, style, and dash pattern.

`dashes` lists 1 to 32 dash and gap lengths in points, which a
`BorderStyle.DASHED` border needs and no other style takes; giving
`dashes` without a style selects the dashed style. A width of 0 draws
no border.

### `BorderStyle`

The style of an annotation's border, `/BS /S` (ISO 32000-2 Table 168).

Members: `SOLID`, `DASHED`, `BEVELED`, `INSET`, `UNDERLINE`.

### `Circle`

```python
Circle(rect: Sequence[float], *, color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), interior_color: Color | None = None, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), clouds: float = 0, opacity: float = 1.0, blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None, contents: str | None = None)
```

An ellipse inscribed in a rectangle, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `Square`; the ellipse and its border lie
inside `rect`.

### `Highlight`

```python
Highlight(rects: MarkupRects, *, color: Color = Color(red=1.0, green=1.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), opacity: float = 0.4, contents: str | None = None)
```

A highlight over text, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`rects` is one rectangle or quad, or a sequence of them, in display
coordinates, such as the result of `page.search`; a `Quad`
contributes its bounding rectangle, and one annotation holds at most
4,096. `color` fills them in multiply blending at `opacity`, and
`contents` is the text of its note. The annotation is written with its
appearance, so every viewer draws it alike.

### `Ink`

```python
Ink(strokes: Iterable[Iterable[Point | Sequence[float]]], *, color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), opacity: float = 1.0, blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None, contents: str | None = None)
```

Freehand strokes, each through one or more display points, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`color` draws every stroke with round caps and joins at the `border`
width; one annotation holds at most 65,536 points in all.

### `LineAnnotation`

```python
LineAnnotation(start: Point | Sequence[float], end: Point | Sequence[float], *, color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), interior_color: Color | None = None, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), line_endings: tuple[LineEnding, LineEnding] = (<LineEnding.NONE: 'none'>, <LineEnding.NONE: 'none'>), opacity: float = 1.0, blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None, contents: str | None = None)
```

A straight line between two display points, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`color` strokes the line with the `border` width and dashes, and
`line_endings` gives the shapes at its start and end, whose closed
shapes `interior_color` fills. The annotation's rectangle is the line's
bounds, widened for the stroke and the endings.

### `LineEnding`

The shape at an end of a line or polyline, `/LE` (ISO 32000-2 Table 179).

Closed shapes are filled with the annotation's interior color.

Members: `NONE`, `SQUARE`, `CIRCLE`, `DIAMOND`, `OPEN_ARROW`, `CLOSED_ARROW`, `BUTT`, `REVERSED_OPEN_ARROW`, `REVERSED_CLOSED_ARROW`, `SLASH`.

### `MarkupRects`

`MarkupRects = collections.abc.Sequence[float] | pyropdf.Quad | collections.abc.Iterable[collections.abc.Sequence[float] | pyropdf.Quad]`

### `Note`

```python
Note(at: Point | Sequence[float], *, contents: str | None = None, icon: NoteIcon = <NoteIcon.NOTE: 'note'>, color: Color = Color(red=1.0, green=1.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), opacity: float = 1.0, is_open: bool = False)
```

A note shown as an icon, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`at` is the display point of the icon's top-left corner; the icon is
20 points square, and its flags ask viewers to keep it upright on a
turned page. `contents` is the note's text, `icon` its picture,
`color` the icon's fill, and `is_open` whether a viewer opens the
note when it shows the page. Add a popup by assigning
`Annotation.popup_rect`.

### `NoteIcon`

The icon of a note, `/Name` (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.4).

Members: `COMMENT`, `HELP`, `INSERT`, `KEY`, `NEW_PARAGRAPH`, `NOTE`, `PARAGRAPH`.

### `Polygon`

```python
Polygon(vertices: Iterable[Point | Sequence[float]], *, color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), interior_color: Color | None = None, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), clouds: float = 0, opacity: float = 1.0, blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None, contents: str | None = None)
```

A closed polygon through two or more display points, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`color` strokes the outline and `interior_color` fills it; `clouds`
from 0 to 2 draws the outline as a cloud whose bumps grow with it. One
annotation holds at most 65,536 points.

### `PolyLine`

```python
PolyLine(vertices: Iterable[Point | Sequence[float]], *, color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), interior_color: Color | None = None, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), line_endings: tuple[LineEnding, LineEnding] = (<LineEnding.NONE: 'none'>, <LineEnding.NONE: 'none'>), opacity: float = 1.0, blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None, contents: str | None = None)
```

An open line through two or more display points, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `LineAnnotation`, with `line_endings` at
the first and last points; one annotation holds at most 65,536 points.

### `Square`

```python
Square(rect: Sequence[float], *, color: Color | None = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), interior_color: Color | None = None, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), clouds: float = 0, opacity: float = 1.0, blend_mode: BlendMode | None = None, contents: str | None = None)
```

A rectangle, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

`rect` is in display coordinates. `color` strokes the border and
`interior_color` fills the inside; either may be `None`. The border
lies inside `rect`, and `clouds` from 0 to 2 draws it as a cloud
whose bumps grow with it, inside `rect` too. `opacity` and
`blend_mode` apply to both paints, and `contents` is the text of the
annotation's note.

### `Squiggly`

```python
Squiggly(rects: MarkupRects, *, color: Color = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), opacity: float = 1.0, contents: str | None = None)
```

A wavy line under text, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `Highlight`; `color` draws a zigzag
two points wide along the bottom of each rectangle, at most 65,536 points
in all (`annotation_point_count`).

### `StampIcon`

The stamps of ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.12, `/Name`; pymupdf's `STAMP_*` codes in their order.

Members: `APPROVED`, `AS_IS`, `CONFIDENTIAL`, `DEPARTMENTAL`, `EXPERIMENTAL`, `EXPIRED`, `FINAL`, `FOR_COMMENT`, `FOR_PUBLIC_RELEASE`, `NOT_APPROVED`, `NOT_FOR_PUBLIC_RELEASE`, `SOLD`, `TOP_SECRET`, `DRAFT`.

### `StrikeOut`

```python
StrikeOut(rects: MarkupRects, *, color: Color = Color(red=1.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), opacity: float = 1.0, contents: str | None = None)
```

A line through text, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `Highlight`; `color` draws a one-point
line through the middle of each rectangle.

### `Underline`

```python
Underline(rects: MarkupRects, *, color: Color = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=1.0, alpha=1.0), opacity: float = 1.0, contents: str | None = None)
```

A line under text, as `page.annotations.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `Highlight`; `color` draws a one-point
line just above the bottom edge of each rectangle.

## Links and destinations

### `Destination`

```python
Destination(page: int, point: Sequence[float] | None = None, zoom: float | None = None)
```

A place in this document: a zero-based page, a point, and a zoom.

`point` is the top left of the view and `zoom` its magnification.
The point is in the page's display coordinates. Without a point or a
zoom the viewer fits the page in the window; `zoom=None` keeps the
viewer's zoom.

### `Destinations`

```python
Destinations(document: Document)
```

The named destinations of a document, as `doc.destinations` returns them.

Keys are the names of the catalog's `/Names /Dests` tree, the first
entry of a repeated name winning, then those of the legacy `/Dests`
dictionary that the tree lacks; a value is the `Destination` the
name leads to, or `None` when it names no page. Links already read
named destinations as the destinations they name. The mapping is
read-only and reads the document on every access, under the
named-destination limits: 65,536 entries or nodes, 131,072 edges
(`named_destination_count`), 32 levels, and 16 MiB of names
(`named_destination_text_size`).

- `__getitem__(name: str) -> Destination | None`: Return where `name` leads; an unknown name raises `KeyError`.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[str]`: Iterate over the names, tree entries first.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of names.

### `Launch`

```python
Launch(file: str)
```

Open a file with the application the viewer associates with it.

### `Link`

```python
Link(page: Page, id: tuple[int, int], index: int)
```

A handle on one link annotation of a page, as `page.links` lists it.

`rect` is the area that follows the link, in the page's display
coordinates, and `target` where it leads; assigning either edits the
annotation. `target` is `None` for an action that pyropdf does not
read, such as JavaScript. A handle reads the document on every access and
names the link's object, so it finds the link again after an edit moved
it; one stored as a direct dictionary in `/Annots` is found by its
position. A handle raises `StaleObjectError` while the link is not
on its page, and `StalePageError` while the page is gone; it works
again if undo restores them.

- `page`: Return the page that holds the link.
- `xref`: Return the annotation's object number, or 0 for a dictionary stored in `/Annots` itself.
- `obj`: Return the annotation dictionary as a live low-level handle.
- `rect` (settable): Return the area that follows the link, in display coordinates.
- `target` (settable): Return where the link leads, or `None` for an action that pyropdf does not read.

### `Links`

```python
Links(page: Page)
```

The link annotations of a page, in `/Annots` order, as `page.links` returns them.

The sequence reads the page on every access. `add(rect, target)` adds
a link and `del page.links[i]` removes one from the page.

Reads reject more than 4,096 annotations or 1 MiB of target text per
page. A named destination resolves through the `/Names /Dests` tree,
which is indexed once until an edit changes what indexing it read, or
the legacy `/Dests` dictionary; a tree beyond 65,536 entries, 16 MiB of
names, or 32 levels raises rather than leaving the link unresolved.

- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Link | list[Link]`: Return one link, or a list of them for a slice.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of links on the page.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[Link]`: Iterate over the links that the page lists now.
- `add(rect: Sequence[float], target: Target) -> Link`: Add a link over `rect`, in display coordinates, that leads to `target`, and return it.

### `NamedAction`

```python
NamedAction(name: str)
```

A viewer action by name (ISO 32000-2 Table 213).

The standard names are `"NextPage"`, `"PrevPage"`, `"FirstPage"`,
and `"LastPage"`; viewers may know others.

### `RemoteDestination`

```python
RemoteDestination(file: str, page: int = 0, name: str | None = None)
```

A place in another PDF file: a zero-based page or a named destination.

### `Target`

`Target = pyropdf.Destination | pyropdf.RemoteDestination | pyropdf.Launch | pyropdf.NamedAction | str`

## Forms and widgets

### `CheckBox`

```python
CheckBox(name: str, rect: Sequence[float], *, checked: bool = False, on_state: str = 'Yes', label: str | None = None, flags: FieldFlags = <FieldFlags: 0>, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), border_color: Color | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), background_color: Color | None = None)
```

A check box, as `page.widgets.add` takes it.

`on_state` names the state that `checked` selects, `"Yes"` by
default; the box draws a check mark in its border.

### `ComboBox`

```python
ComboBox(name: str, rect: Sequence[float], *, choices: Iterable[FieldChoice | str], value: str | None = None, default_value: str | None = None, font_size: float = 0, text_color: Color = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] = 'left', label: str | None = None, flags: FieldFlags = <FieldFlags: 0>, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), border_color: Color | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), background_color: Color | None = None)
```

A drop-down choice field, as `page.widgets.add` takes it.

`choices` are `FieldChoice` records or strings; `flags` with
`FieldFlags.EDIT` also takes typed text. The value is drawn as in a
`TextField`.

### `Field`

```python
Field(document: Document, xref: int, generation: int)
```

A handle on one terminal form field, as `doc.form[name]` returns it.

Properties read the document on every access. A handle names its field's
object and raises `StaleObjectError` while that object is no
terminal field of the form; it works again if undo restores it.

- `xref`: Return the field dictionary's object number.
- `obj`: Return the field dictionary in the low-level object model.
- `name`: Return the fully qualified name, the partial names of the field and its ancestors joined by dots.
- `type`: Return the field's kind.
- `flags` (settable): Return or set the field flags, inherited from ancestors that set `/Ff`; undefined bits are dropped.
- `choices` (settable): Return or set a choice field's options in `/Opt` order, or `()` without them.
- `label` (settable): Return or set the field's description for users, `/TU`; `del` removes it.
- `max_length` (settable): Return or set the most characters that a text field holds, `/MaxLen`; `del` removes it.
- `default_value` (settable): Return or set the value that `reset` restores, `/DV`; `del` removes it.
- `reset()`: Restore the field's default value, or clear its value, and draw its widgets again.
- `is_signed`: Return whether this is a signature field whose value is a signature dictionary.
- `widgets`: Return the widgets that show the field, in page order, each a `Widget` handle.
- `value` (settable): Return the field's value.
- `scripts`: Return the field's JavaScript by trigger: keystroke, format, validate, and calculate.

### `FieldChoice`

```python
FieldChoice(value: str, label: str)
```

One option of a choice field's `/Opt`.

### `FieldFlags`

The field flags of `/Ff` (ISO 32000-2 Tables 227, 229, 231, and 233).

Bits 26 and 27 mean different things for buttons and for text and choice
fields, so `RADIOS_IN_UNISON` is the same bit as `RICH_TEXT`.

Members: `READ_ONLY`, `REQUIRED`, `NO_EXPORT`, `MULTILINE`, `PASSWORD`, `NO_TOGGLE_TO_OFF`, `RADIO`, `PUSHBUTTON`, `COMBO`, `EDIT`, `SORT`, `FILE_SELECT`, `MULTI_SELECT`, `DO_NOT_SPELL_CHECK`, `DO_NOT_SCROLL`, `COMB`, `RICH_TEXT`, `COMMIT_ON_SEL_CHANGE`.

### `FieldSpecification`

`FieldSpecification = pyropdf.TextField | pyropdf.CheckBox | pyropdf.RadioButton | pyropdf.ComboBox | pyropdf.ListBox | pyropdf.PushButton | pyropdf.SignatureField`

### `FieldType`

The kind of a form field, from its `/FT` and the flags that refine it.

Members: `TEXT`, `CHECKBOX`, `RADIO`, `PUSHBUTTON`, `COMBOBOX`, `LISTBOX`, `SIGNATURE`, `UNKNOWN`.

### `Form`

```python
Form(document: Document)
```

The terminal fields of a document's interactive form, as `doc.form` returns them.

Keys are fully qualified field names in sorted order; when malformed
files give two fields one name, the mapping holds the first by object
number. A document without a form is an empty mapping. Reads refuse
more than 4,096 fields or tree nodes, 8,192 edges, 64 levels, 4,096
widgets, 1 MiB of names or values, or 4,096 value items with
`PdfError` rather than return part of the form.

- `repair_radio_groups() -> int`: Gather top-level radio buttons that share a name under one field, and return how many groups it made.
- `signature_flags`: Return the AcroForm's `/SigFlags`, without undefined bits; a document without a form reads none.
- `need_appearances` (settable): Return or set the AcroForm's `/NeedAppearances`, which asks viewers to draw the widgets again.
- `__getitem__(name: str) -> Field`: Return the field named `name`; another name raises `KeyError`.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[str]`: Iterate over the field names in sorted order.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of distinct field names.

### `ListBox`

```python
ListBox(name: str, rect: Sequence[float], *, choices: Iterable[FieldChoice | str], value: str | None = None, default_value: str | None = None, font_size: float = 0, text_color: Color = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] = 'left', label: str | None = None, flags: FieldFlags = <FieldFlags: 0>, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), border_color: Color | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), background_color: Color | None = None)
```

A list of choices, as `page.widgets.add` takes it.

The fields are those of `ComboBox`; `FieldFlags.MULTI_SELECT`
lets the user select several.

### `PushButton`

```python
PushButton(name: str, rect: Sequence[float], *, caption: str | None = None, font_size: float = 0, text_color: Color = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), label: str | None = None, flags: FieldFlags = <FieldFlags: 0>, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), border_color: Color | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), background_color: Color | None = Color(red=0.75, green=0.75, blue=0.75, alpha=1.0))
```

A pushbutton, which holds no value, as `page.widgets.add` takes it.

`caption` is drawn centred in Helvetica at `font_size` in
`text_color`.

### `RadioButton`

```python
RadioButton(name: str, rect: Sequence[float], *, on_state: str, selected: bool = False, label: str | None = None, flags: FieldFlags = <FieldFlags: 0>, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), border_color: Color | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), background_color: Color | None = None)
```

One button of a radio group, as `page.widgets.add` takes it.

Buttons that share `name` form one group, each selecting its own
`on_state`; `selected` selects this one.

### `Scripts`

```python
Scripts(document: Document, holder: Callable[[], Dictionary], triggers: frozenset[ScriptTrigger])
```

The JavaScript of a field or widget by trigger, as `field.scripts` and `widget.scripts` return them.

Keys are `ScriptTrigger` members and values the script source;
assigning sets a JavaScript action, and `del` removes it, each in one
transaction. Actions of other kinds are not listed. A field takes the
keystroke, format, validate, and calculate triggers, and a widget the
others. pyropdf never runs the scripts. Each script and the mapping's
scripts together stop at 1 MiB of UTF-8 (`script_size`); a refused
write changes nothing.

- `__getitem__(trigger: ScriptTrigger) -> str`: Return the script of `trigger`; a trigger without one raises `KeyError`.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[ScriptTrigger]`: Iterate over the triggers that have a script.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of scripts.

### `ScriptTrigger`

When a viewer runs a form script: the field triggers of `field.scripts`, the widget ones of `widget.scripts`.

pyropdf stores scripts and never runs them.

Members: `KEYSTROKE`, `FORMAT`, `VALIDATE`, `CALCULATE`, `FOCUS`, `BLUR`, `ENTER`, `EXIT`, `DOWN`, `UP`, `ACTIVATE`.

### `SignatureField`

```python
SignatureField(name: str, rect: Sequence[float], *, label: str | None = None, flags: FieldFlags = <FieldFlags: 0>, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), border_color: Color | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), background_color: Color | None = None)
```

An unsigned signature field, which a signing tool such as pyHanko fills, as `page.widgets.add` takes it.

### `SignatureFlags`

The signature flags of the AcroForm's `/SigFlags` (ISO 32000-2 Table 225), which signing tools set.

Members: `SIGNATURES_EXIST`, `APPEND_ONLY`.

### `TextField`

```python
TextField(name: str, rect: Sequence[float], *, value: str | None = None, default_value: str | None = None, max_length: int | None = None, font_size: float = 0, text_color: Color = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] = 'left', label: str | None = None, flags: FieldFlags = <FieldFlags: 0>, border: Border = Border(width=1.0, style=<BorderStyle.SOLID: 'solid'>, dashes=()), border_color: Color | None = Color(red=0.0, green=0.0, blue=0.0, alpha=1.0), background_color: Color | None = None)
```

A text field, or another widget of the text field of that name, as `page.widgets.add` takes it.

`rect` is in display coordinates. `value` and `default_value` are
the field's text, drawn in Helvetica at `font_size` (0 fits the text),
in `text_color`, aligned by `align`. `flags` adds
`FieldFlags` such as `MULTILINE`, `PASSWORD`, `COMB`,
`REQUIRED`, or `READ_ONLY`; `max_length` bounds the text.

### `Widget`

```python
Widget(page: Page, id: tuple[int, int], index: int)
```

A handle on one form widget of a page, as `page.widgets` lists it.

Properties read the document on every access, and assigning one changes
the widget and draws it again for its field's value, in one
transaction. A handle finds its widget again after an edit moved it; it
raises `StaleObjectError` while the widget is not on its page and
`StalePageError` while the page is gone, and it works again if
undo restores them.

- `page`: Return the page that shows the widget.
- `xref`: Return the widget's object number, or 0 for a dictionary stored in `/Annots` itself.
- `obj`: Return the widget dictionary as a live low-level handle.
- `scripts`: Return the widget's JavaScript by trigger: focus, blur, enter, exit, down, up, and activate.
- `field`: Return the terminal form field that the widget shows, or `None` when no field owns it.
- `rect` (settable): Return or set the widget rectangle in display coordinates.
- `flags` (settable): Return or set the widget's `/F` flags, such as `AnnotationFlags.HIDDEN`.
- `border` (settable): Return or set the border, `/BS` else `/Border`; `del` removes it.
- `border_color` (settable): Return or set the border color, `/MK /BC`; `del` removes it.
- `background_color` (settable): Return or set the background color, `/MK /BG`; `del` removes it.
- `caption` (settable): Return or set the caption of a pushbutton, `/MK /CA`; `del` removes it.
- `rotation` (settable): Return or set the rotation of the widget's appearance, `/MK /R`: 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees.
- `text_color` (settable): Return or set the color of the widget's text, from the `/DA` that it draws with.
- `font_size` (settable): Return or set the size of the widget's text in points, 0 to fit the text to the widget.
- `button_states`: Return the appearance states of a check box or radio button, such as `("Off", "Yes")`.
- `on_state`: Return the state that selects a check box or radio button, or `None` without one.

### `Widgets`

```python
Widgets(page: Page)
```

The form widgets of a page, as `page.widgets` returns them, in `/Annots` order.

Reads reject more than 4,096 annotations or 1 MiB of state names per
page.

- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Widget | list[Widget]`: Return one widget, or a list of them for a slice.
- `add(specification: FieldSpecification) -> Widget`: Add the widget that `specification` describes, and return it.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of widgets on the page.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[Widget]`: Iterate over the widgets that the page lists now.

## Outline

### `Outline`

```python
Outline(document: Document)
```

The document's outline as its top-level items, as `doc.outline` returns it.

Each item's `children` give the rest of the tree, and `walk`
visits every item in document order. Assigning a list of
`OutlineEntry` records to `doc.outline` replaces the outline,
and `del doc.outline` removes it. The view reads the document on every
access.

- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> OutlineItem | list[OutlineItem]`: Return a top-level item, or a list of them for a slice.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of top-level items.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[OutlineItem]`: Iterate over the top-level items.
- `walk() -> Iterator[OutlineItem]`: Iterate over every item in document order, each before its children.
- `entries() -> list[OutlineEntry]`: Return every item in document order as `OutlineEntry` records.

### `OutlineEntry`

```python
OutlineEntry(level: int, title: str, destination: Target | None = None, *, color: Color | None = None, bold: bool = False, italic: bool = False, is_open: bool = False)
```

One item of an outline to write, as `doc.outline = [...]` takes it.

Levels start at 1 and grow by at most one from one entry to the next; an
entry's children are the entries of the next level that follow it.
`is_open` shows the children when the document opens.

- `page`: Return the zero-based page of a `Destination`, else `None`.

### `OutlineItem`

```python
OutlineItem(document: Document, xref: int, generation: int)
```

A handle on one item of the outline, as `doc.outline` yields it.

Properties read the document on every access, and assigning `title`,
`destination`, `color`, `bold`, `italic`, or `is_open` edits the
item at once. A handle raises `StaleObjectError` while its item no
longer exists, as after the outline is replaced; it works again if undo
restores it.

- `xref`: Return the item's object number.
- `obj`: Return the item's dictionary in the low-level object model.
- `level`: Return the item's depth: 1 for a top-level item.
- `title` (settable): Return the title shown in the viewer's outline.
- `destination` (settable): Return where the item leads, or `None`.
- `page`: Return the zero-based page of a `Destination`, else `None`.
- `color` (settable): Return the title's color, or `None` for the viewer's default.
- `bold` (settable): Return whether the title shows in bold.
- `italic` (settable): Return whether the title shows in italic.
- `is_open` (settable): Return whether the item's children show; `False` without children.
- `children`: Return the item's children in order.
- `to_entry() -> OutlineEntry`: Return the item, without its children, as an `OutlineEntry`.

## Attachments

### `Attachment`

```python
Attachment(document: Document, name: str)
```

A handle on one embedded file of a document, as `doc.attachments[name]` returns it.

Properties read the document on every access. A handle raises
`StaleObjectError` once its attachment has been deleted.

- `name`: Return the key under which the document lists the attachment.
- `filename`: Return the viewer-facing file name (`/UF`, else `/F`), or `""`.
- `description`: Return the description (`/Desc`), or `None`.
- `size`: Return the uncompressed size that the file declares (`/Params /Size`), or -1, as pymupdf does.
- `created`: Return the creation date (`/Params /CreationDate`) as stored, or `None`.
- `modified`: Return the modification date (`/Params /ModDate`) as stored, or `None`; `write` sets it.
- `read(*, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> bytes`: Return the attachment's contents, as pymupdf's `embfile_get` does.
- `write(data: bytes, /, *, max_size: int | None = 67108864)`: Replace the attachment's contents, as pymupdf's `embfile_upd` does with `buffer_`.

### `Attachments`

```python
Attachments(document: Document)
```

The embedded files of a document, keyed by name, as `doc.attachments` returns them.

This live view replaces pymupdf's `embfile_*` methods: iterate it for
the sorted names, index it for an `Attachment`, `add` a file, and
`del` one. The EmbeddedFiles name tree is read within its bounds on
every access.

- `__getitem__(name: str) -> Attachment`: Return the handle of the attachment called `name`; raise `KeyError` when absent.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[str]`: Iterate the attachment names in sorted order.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of attachments, as pymupdf's `embfile_count` does.
- `add(name: str, data: bytes, /, *, filename: str | None = None, description: str | None = None, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> Attachment`: Add an attachment and return its handle, as pymupdf's `embfile_add` does.

## History and changes

### `ChangeReport`

```python
ChangeReport(signatures: tuple[SignatureChange, ...], claims: tuple[ClaimChange, ...])
```

What the edits since opening invalidate, for a save that is incremental or not.

### `ClaimChange`

```python
ClaimChange(claim: str, reason: str, objects: tuple[int, ...])
```

A PDF/A or PDF/UA claim of the metadata that the edits break.

`claim` names it, such as `"PDF/A-1B"` or `"PDF/UA-1"`, and
`objects` lists the edited objects that break it. The report checks
what the edits wrote, not the whole document against the claim: added
transparency and embedded files break PDF/A-1, an embedded file that is
not PDF/A-1 or PDF/A-2 breaks PDF/A-2, one that is not PDF/A-1, -2, or -4
breaks PDF/A-4 but not PDF/A-4f, and untagged annotations break PDF/UA.

### `History`

```python
History(document: Document)
```

The line of steps that undo and redo walk (DESIGN.md section 4.1).

Every committed edit is a step: a transaction is one step with its name,
and an edit outside a transaction is one step named `""`. A new step
after undo discards the redo steps. `max_size` bounds the bytes
that the steps keep, 256 MiB by default: the farthest redo steps go
first while redo alone is over it, then the oldest undo steps.

- `steps`: Return the names of the steps, oldest first: those that undo and then redo can take.
- `position`: Return how many steps undo can take.
- `can_undo`: Return whether a step can be undone.
- `can_redo`: Return whether a step can be redone.
- `size`: Return the bytes that the steps keep, as the budget counts them.
- `max_size` (settable): Return the budget of the steps in bytes, or `None` for no limit; 0 keeps no step.
- `undo()`: Undo one step; raises `PdfError` with nothing to undo or inside a transaction.
- `redo()`: Redo one step; raises `PdfError` with nothing to redo or inside a transaction.
- `clear()`: Forget every step, keeping the document as it is.

### `SignatureChange`

```python
SignatureChange(field: str, xref: int, reason: str, objects: tuple[int, ...])
```

A signature of the opened file that the edits or the save mode invalidate.

`field` is the signature field's full name and `xref` its object.
`objects` lists the edited objects that the signature signs, empty when
the save mode alone invalidates it.

### `Transaction`

```python
Transaction(document: Document, name: str)
```

A group of edits that commits as one version and one undo step.

`with doc.transaction(name):` opens it. Leaving the block commits its
edits; an exception discards them, without copying the document, and
propagates. A transaction opened inside another joins it: its edits
commit with the outer one, and its exception discards only its own
edits. Reads inside the block see its edits.

A transaction belongs to the thread that opened it. Other threads read
the version before it until it commits, and their edits, transactions,
undo, and redo wait until it ends.

## Encryption

### `Access`

What a password opened: the user's restricted access, or the owner's full access.

Members: `USER`, `OWNER`.

### `Encryption`

```python
Encryption(*, user_password: str = '', owner_password: str | None = None, permissions: Permissions = <Permissions.ALL: 3900>, method: Literal['aes-256', 'aes-128', 'keep'] = 'aes-256')
```

How `Document.save` and `Document.to_bytes` encrypt a full save.

The user password opens the document with the rights in `permissions`,
and the owner password opens it with every right. `owner_password`
defaults to `user_password`. Each password is capped at 127 UTF-8 bytes.

`method` is `"aes-256"`, the AES-256 encryption of PDF 2.0 (revision
6), or `"aes-128"`, AES-128 with crypt filters (revision 4). pyropdf
reads RC4 but never writes it. `Encryption.KEEP` keeps the
encryption that the document was opened with, copying its untouched
encrypted bytes. Without `encryption`, a full save writes the document
decrypted, and an incremental save keeps its encryption.

### `Permissions`

What an encrypted document permits the user password, combined with `|`.

`Document.permissions` reports them and `Encryption(permissions=)`
sets them. The values are the `/P` bits of ISO 32000-2 Table 22, and
`ALL` combines every member.

Members: `PRINT`, `MODIFY`, `COPY`, `ANNOTATE`, `FORM`, `ACCESSIBILITY`, `ASSEMBLE`, `PRINT_HQ`.

## Limits and errors

### `CancellationToken`

A flag that stops the operations of every document whose limits carry it.

Any thread may call `cancel`, also while another thread's
operation runs with the GIL released: the operation then refuses with
`LimitError` code `cancelled` at its next check. Cancelling
cannot be undone, so a document whose token is cancelled refuses every
later operation too; open it again with another token to go on.

- `cancel()`: Cancels every operation whose limits carry this token.
- `cancelled`: Whether `cancel` was called.

### `DocumentClosedError`

An operation on a closed document.

### `DocumentLimits`

```python
DocumentLimits(*, max_file_size: int | None = None, max_pages: int | None = None, max_objects: int | None = None, max_decompressed_size: int | None = None, max_page_content_size: int | None = None, max_total_decompressed_size: int | None = None, max_object_depth: int | None = None, max_interpretation_size: int | None = None, max_duration: float | None = None, cancellation: CancellationToken | None = None, check_at_open: bool = False)
```

Optional budgets for opening and reading PDFs.

`None` leaves a limit unset. Each limit refuses with `LimitError`,
whose `code` names it. Opening reads only the cross-reference data, so
damage and most limits surface when a part is first read;
`check_at_open` reads every object at open instead. `web` is a
conservative profile for servers that read documents in bounded workers.

- `web() -> DocumentLimits`: Return pylopdf's web profile, which checks every object at open.

### `EncryptedDocumentError`

An operation on an encrypted document that needs a password.

### `LimitError`

A refusal by a limit, whose `code` names the limit.

- `code`: The stable code of the limit, from `LIMIT_CODES`.

### `MalformedPdfError`

Input that cannot be read as a PDF document, including empty input.

### `OcrError`

OCR model loading or inference failed.

### `PasswordError`

A password that matches neither the user password nor the owner password.

### `PdfError`

The base class of the errors that pyropdf raises for a document.

### `PyropdfWarning`

A recoverable condition of reading a PDF, such as glyphs that text extraction left out.

### `StaleObjectError`

Use of a handle whose object the current version no longer has.

### `StalePageError`

Use of a `Page` whose page object the page tree no longer lists.

Other pages' edits never make a page stale; deleting it does, and undo
can make it valid again. Fetch a current page with `doc.pages[i]`.

## Content operations

### `InlineImage`

```python
InlineImage(dictionary: Mapping[str, Any], data: bytes)
```

An inline image: its dictionary, keyed by name text as written, and its data.

The dictionary keeps the abbreviations of ISO 32000-2 §8.9.7 as the
stream wrote them (`W`, `H`, `BPC`, `CS`, `F`), and `data`
holds the bytes between `ID` and `EI`, still encoded with the
dictionary's filters, without the white-space byte before `EI`, which
writing adds back.

- `operator`: Return `"BI"`, so that every item of `Operations` has an operator.
- `operands`: Return `()`: an inline image holds its dictionary and data instead.

### `Operation`

```python
Operation(operator: str, operands: tuple[Any, ...] = ())
```

One content-stream operation: an operator and its operands.

`operator` is the operator's text, such as `"Tj"` or `"cm"`.
`operands` holds the values that precede it, as the object model reads
them: `None`, `bool`, `int`, `Real`, `Name`,
`String`, tuples for arrays, and dictionaries keyed by name text.
A plain `str` operand is written as a text string, as in the object
model; write `String` or `bytes` for the bytes that a font
shows.

### `Operations`

```python
Operations(items: Iterable[Operation | InlineImage] = (), *, tail: bytes = b'')
```

An immutable sequence of content-stream operations.

`Operations.parse(data)` reads a content stream as hayro tokenizes it,
and `to_bytes()` writes it back: operations that the parse produced
write their original bytes, comments and white space included, so
`Operations.parse(data).to_bytes() == data`, and new operations are
written from their values. Bytes after the last operation that hayro
reads, such as content after an operation that it cannot read, stay in
`tail` and are written last.

- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Operation | InlineImage | Operations`: Return one operation, or the operations of a slice without the tail.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[Operation | InlineImage]`: Iterate over the operations.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of operations.
- `parse(data: bytes, /, *, max_operations: int | None = 1048576, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> Operations`: Read a decoded content stream, such as a Form XObject's `Stream.read()`.
- `tail`: Return the bytes after the last operation.
- `to_bytes() -> bytes`: Write the operations as content-stream bytes.

## Objects

### `Array`

A PDF array; elements resolve and write as `Dictionary` values do.

- `__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Any`: Return the resolved element at `index`, or a list for a slice.
- `insert(index: int, value: object)`: Insert `value` before `index`, clamped as `list.insert` clamps it.

### `Dictionary`

A PDF dictionary keyed by name text without the slash.

Reading a key resolves references: an array, dictionary, or stream comes
back as a handle, and anything else as a plain value. Assigning a value
writes it at once, in one transaction. Plain values, lists, and mappings
are written as direct objects; an indirect handle from the same document
is written as a reference to it; and a direct handle is copied.

- `__getitem__(key: str) -> Any`: Return the resolved value of `key`.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[str]`: Iterate over the keys as `Name` values.

### `Name`

A PDF name, such as `/Type`, held without its leading slash.

A name compares equal to the plain string of its text, so
`page.obj["Type"] == "Page"` holds. Writing needs the type, though: a
plain `str` value is written as a PDF text string, so write
`Name("Page")` for a name. Bytes that are not UTF-8 are kept as
surrogate escapes, so a name read from a file is written back unchanged.

### `Objects`

```python
Objects(document: Document)
```

The indirect objects of a document, keyed by object number.

Look up `doc.objects[xref]` to read an object, assign to replace it,
and call `add` or `add_stream` to create one. An object that
is an array, dictionary, or stream comes back as a handle; any other as
its value. Assigning a handle here copies what it addresses, so
`doc.objects[target] = doc.objects[source]` copies an object, whereas
assigning an indirect handle inside a container writes a reference.

- `__getitem__(xref: int) -> Any`: Return the object stored under `xref`.
- `__iter__() -> Iterator[int]`: Iterate over object numbers in ascending order.
- `__len__() -> int`: Return the number of object numbers in use.
- `add(value: object) -> int`: Add `value` as a new indirect object, in one transaction, and return its object number.
- `add_stream(data: bytes, /, dictionary: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, *, filter: Literal['FlateDecode'] | None = 'FlateDecode') -> int`: Add a stream of decoded `data`, in one transaction, and return its object number.

### `Real`

A PDF real: a `float` that keeps the digits it is written with.

A real read from a document is a `Real`, and so equal to, hashed as,
and computed with as its `float` value; arithmetic returns a plain
`float`. `lexeme` is the bytes that the real is written with,
when they are known, and travels with the value through copies, other
documents, and `pickle`. `Real("35.68123456789012345")` and
`Real(Decimal(...))` keep digits beyond a `float`'s precision;
`Real(1.5)` has no lexeme and is written in the shortest form that
reads back as its `float`. As DESIGN.md section 10 says, assigning a
`Real` writes its lexeme, a `float` its shortest form, and a
`Decimal` its exact digits.

- `lexeme`: Return the bytes that the real is written with, or `None` when only its `float` is known.
- `to_decimal() -> Decimal`: Return the exact decimal that the real is written as.

### `Stream`

A PDF stream: its dictionary, plus `read` and `write`.

- `read(*, decode: bool = True, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> bytes`: Return the stream data, decoded through its filters unless `decode` is false.
- `write(data: bytes, /, *, filter: Literal['FlateDecode'] | None = 'FlateDecode')`: Replace the stream data with `data`, given decoded, in one transaction.

### `String`

A PDF string: its bytes, with `text` decoding a text string.

Write a `str` to store a text string (ASCII as is, anything else as
UTF-16BE), or `bytes` or a `String` to store the bytes exactly.

- `text`: Decode the bytes as a PDF text string.

## Geometry

### `IRect`

An immutable integer rectangle `(x0, y0, x1, y1)`.

Accept the same arguments as `Rect`. Fractional coordinates
move outward: `x0` and `y0` round down and `x1` and `y1` round
up, also for the results of arithmetic. The operators and members are
those of `Rect`, apart from `abs()`, truth testing, and
`round()`, which pymupdf's IRect does not define.

- `height`: Return `y1 - y0`, or 0 when that is negative.
- `rect`: Return the same rectangle as a `Rect`.
- `width`: Return `x1 - x0`, or 0 when that is negative.

### `Matrix`

An immutable affine matrix `(a, b, c, d, e, f)`.

Construct the zero matrix with no arguments, scaling with `(sx, sy)`,
rotation with an angle in degrees, shear with `(sx, sy, 1)`, or an
explicit matrix with six coordinates or a six-item sequence.
`Matrix(sx, sy, 0)` also constructs scaling. Coordinate keywords
`a` through `f` may be used when all six coordinates are supplied.

`left * right` applies `left` first. `~matrix` returns the inverse,
or the zero matrix for a singular matrix. Division by a singular matrix
raises `ZeroDivisionError`. Coordinates must be finite.

- `is_rectilinear`: Return whether axis-aligned rectangles remain axis-aligned.
- `norm() -> float`: Return the Euclidean norm of all six coordinates.
- `planish(p1: Sequence[float], p2: Sequence[float]) -> Matrix`: Return the matrix that moves `p1` to the origin and `p2` onto the positive x axis.

### `Point`

An immutable point `(x, y)` in display coordinates.

Accept two coordinates, a two-item sequence, or no arguments for the
origin. `+` and `-` add or subtract coordinates; `*` and `/`
scale by a number or apply a matrix and its inverse. Coordinates must
be finite. Tuple indexing, unpacking, equality, and hashing remain.

- `abs_unit`: Return the direction vector with nonnegative coordinates.
- `distance_to(x: Sequence[float], unit: str = 'px') -> float`: Measure distance to a point or normalized rectangle.
- `norm() -> float`: Return the distance from the origin.
- `unit`: Return the direction vector of length one, or the origin for zero.

### `Quad`

An immutable quadrilateral of four corner points `(ul, ur, ll, lr)`.

Accept four points, a four-item sequence of points such as another
quad, the coordinate keywords `ul`, `ur`, `ll`, and `lr`
together, or no arguments for four origin points. A rectangle's quad
is `rect.quad`. `+` and `-` add or subtract a scalar or another
quad's corners; `*` and `/` scale or transform every corner by a
matrix and its inverse; `in` tests containment. Tuple indexing,
unpacking, equality, and hashing remain.

- `height`: Return the longer of the left and right edges.
- `is_convex`: Return whether the outline `ul, ur, lr, ll` encloses a convex area.
- `is_empty`: Return whether `width` or `height` is below 1e-5.
- `is_infinite`: Return whether the bounding rectangle is infinite.
- `is_rectangular`: Return whether every corner is a right angle, turning as `Rect.quad` does.
- `morph(p: Sequence[float], m: Sequence[float]) -> Quad`: Transform the corners by `m` around the fixed point `p`.
- `rect`: Return the smallest rectangle that contains the four corners.
- `width`: Return the longer of the top and bottom edges.

### `Rect`

An immutable rectangle `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in display coordinates.

Accept four coordinates, a four-item sequence such as another
rectangle, two corner points, a top-left point and `x1, y1`,
`x0, y0` and a bottom-right point, or no arguments for the zero
rectangle. `+` and `-` add or subtract a scalar or rectangle; `*`
and `/` scale or transform by a matrix and its inverse; `|`
includes a point or rectangle; `&` intersects; `in` tests
containment. `width` and `height` are never negative. Coordinates
must be finite. Tuple indexing, unpacking, equality, and hashing remain.

- `irect`: Return `round`.
- `round() -> IRect`: Return the smallest integer rectangle that covers this one.

## Checks and profiles

### `OutputIntent`

```python
OutputIntent(subtype: str | None, identifier: str | None, condition: str | None, registry: str | None, info: str | None, profile: int | None)
```

One entry of the catalog's `/OutputIntents`.

`subtype` is `/S` without its slash, such as `"GTS_PDFA1"`, and
`profile` the xref of `/DestOutputProfile`, or `None`. A text entry
that is missing, or neither a string nor a name, is `None`.

### `Profiles`

```python
Profiles(pdfa: str | None, pdfua: str | None, pdfx: str | None, pdfvt: str | None, output_intents: tuple[OutputIntent, ...])
```

The profile claims of a document's XMP metadata, and its output intents.

Each claim is a name such as `"PDF/A-2B"`, `"PDF/UA-1"`,
`"PDF/X-4"`, or `"PDF/VT-1"`, or `None` when the metadata does not
declare it. A claim is what the document says of itself; whether it
holds is for a validator such as veraPDF to decide.

### `StructuralDefect`

```python
StructuralDefect(xref: int | None, path: str, clause: str, spec: str, kind: DefectKind, message: str)
```

One departure of the document from the model.

`xref` is the indirect object, or `None` for the trailer, and `path`
the keys and indexes from that object to the value, joined by `/`.
`clause` is the Arlington clause, the object type and key such as
`"Catalog/Pages"`, and `spec` the clause of ISO 32000 that the model
names, such as `"Table 29"`, or an empty string.

### `StructuralReport`

```python
StructuralReport(defects: tuple[StructuralDefect, ...], version: str, objects: int, unchecked: int, truncated: bool)
```

What the structural check found.

`version` is the PDF version that the check held the document to: the
later of its header and the catalog's `/Version`. `objects` counts
the indirect objects that the walk reached, and `unchecked` the
predicates of the model that it met but cannot decide. `truncated` is
whether defects past the report's limit were dropped.

## Typed objects

### `pyropdf.typed`

Typed views of PDF objects, one per object type of the Arlington PDF Model.

DESIGN.md section 8: the descriptors that pyropdf-schema generates from the
model give each key of an object type its types, the object types it links
to, whether it is required or inheritable, its default, and its possible
values. A view reads and writes a `pyropdf.Dictionary`,
`pyropdf.Stream`, or `pyropdf.Array` handle by those rules::

    catalog = typed.Catalog(doc.catalog)
    root = catalog.Pages              # a PageTreeNodeRoot view
    page = typed.PageObject(doc.pages[0].obj)
    page.Rotate                       # inherited from the page tree, else 0
    page.Rotate = 90                  # checked against the declared types

Each object type is a subclass of `View` named after it; a name that
begins with `3D` begins with `ThreeD` instead. An attribute reads or
writes a key whose name is an identifier, and indexing reads or writes any
key or array element. Reading converts a value to its declared type:

- `integer` and `bitmask` read as `int`, `number` as `int` or
  `pyropdf.Real`, and `boolean` as `bool`;
- `name` reads as `pyropdf.Name`; `string-text`,
  `string-ascii`, and `date` as `str`; `string` and `string-byte`
  as `pyropdf.String`;
- `rectangle` reads as a tuple of four floats as stored, and `matrix` as
  a `pyropdf.Matrix`;
- a container that links to object types reads as the view of the linked
  type that its `/Type`-like keys match, a container that links to none
  as its handle, and `name-tree` and `number-tree` as their dictionary.

An inheritable key absent from its object is read from the nearest
`/Parent` that holds it, and a key absent everywhere reads as its default
when the model gives one. An absent optional key reads as `None` through an
attribute, and a `null` value counts as absent (ISO 32000-2 section 7.3.7).
A required key that is absent, and a value of no declared type, raise
`pyropdf.PdfError`. Predicates of the model are not evaluated here;
the structural check evaluates them.

Writing takes the Python form of a declared type, or a view or handle for a
container type, and refuses anything else with `TypeError`, or a name
outside the key's possible values with `ValueError`. Assigning `None` to
an attribute removes the key, unless the key may be `null`.

`typed.pyi`, which tools/arlington/generate.py writes, declares each view's
keys with their types for type checkers.
